MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If y = 3, what is the value of 8 − y? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 83
   C. 24
   D. 5

2. If n = 6, what is the value of n + 5? (1 mark)
   A. 65
   B. 11
   C. 30
   D. 1

3. Which expression shows "a number y shared equally among 4 people"? (1 mark)
   A. 4y
   B. y ÷ 4
   C. y + 4
   D. y − 4

4. A pencil starts at the 5 cm mark on a ruler and ends at the 10 cm mark. How long is the pencil? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. 5 cm
   C. 6 cm
   D. 15 cm

5. What is 4 m 60 cm + 1 m 75 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 6 m 35 cm
   B. 6 m 25 cm
   C. 7 m 35 cm
   D. 5 m 35 cm

6. What is 1.2 m in centimetres? (1 mark)
   A. 102 cm
   B. 12 cm
   C. 120 cm
   D. 1,200 cm

7. A rectangle is made of 3 rows with 5 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 15 square units
   B. 18 square units
   C. 8 square units
   D. 16 square units

8. A garden bed marked in 1 m squares has 9 rows and 4 columns. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 26 square metres
   B. 49 square metres
   C. 36 square metres
   D. 13 square metres

9. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. They are equal
   B. Rectangle Q
   C. It cannot be told
   D. Rectangle P

10. A cuboid is 4 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 64 blocks
   B. 16 blocks
   C. 12 blocks
   D. 68 blocks

11. A cuboid has a volume of 72 blocks. One layer has 24 blocks. How many layers are there? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 96
   C. 4
   D. 48

12. A box is 10 cm long, 10 cm wide and 10 cm high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 300 cubic centimetres
   B. 100 cubic centimetres
   C. 30 cubic centimetres
   D. 1,000 cubic centimetres

13. What is 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 L
   B. 4 1/4 L
   C. 3 1/2 L
   D. 3 3/4 L

14. What is 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 L
   B. 3 3/4 L
   C. 4 L
   D. 3 1/2 L

15. An electronic balance shows 0.75 kg. Which mass is this? (1 mark)
   A. 1/2 kg
   B. 3/4 kg
   C. 1/4 kg
   D. 7 1/2 kg

16. Two 1/4 kg masses balance (1 mark)
   A. 1/4 kg
   B. 1 kg
   C. 3/4 kg
   D. 1/2 kg

17. What is 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 4 1/4 kg
   B. 3 3/4 kg
   C. 4 kg
   D. 3 1/2 kg

18. a.m. is used for times (1 mark)
   A. only at midday
   B. only at night
   C. from midnight to noon
   D. from noon to midnight

19. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 3 h
   B. 3 h 30 min
   C. 2 h
   D. 2 h 30 min

20. How many days are in 2 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 48 days
   B. 14 days
   C. 10 days
   D. 21 days

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A trader has 25 kg of rice. She sells 7 1/2 kg to one customer and 6 3/4 kg to another. How much rice does she have left? (5 marks)

22. Explain the difference between area and volume. (2 marks)

23. A trader has 12 kg of beans and 8 kg of maize. He sells 5 kg of the beans. Find the total mass of the beans and maize he has left. (3 marks)

24. A learner says the volume of a cuboid 4 blocks long, 3 wide and 2 high is 9 blocks because 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. What mistake did the learner make and what is the correct volume? (3 marks)

25. Mama Kioko sells 3 bags of mangoes (m) and 2 bags of oranges (o) on Monday, then 1 bag of mangoes and 4 bags of oranges on Tuesday. Write an expression and simplify it. (4 marks)

26. Write these times using a.m. or p.m.: (a) waking up at half past six in the morning, (b) school ending at a quarter past three in the afternoon, (c) supper at half past seven at night. (3 marks)

27. Change 250 cm to metres and centimetres, and then to metres using a decimal. (3 marks)

28. A bag has a mass of 5 kg. Musa takes out 1 1/2 kg of beans. What mass is left in the bag? (2 marks)

29. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes, and change 35 days to weeks. (3 marks)

30. A film begins at 4:20 p.m. and runs for 1 hour 40 minutes. Find the time at which it ends. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #14 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 5
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 5.

2. B — 11
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 11.

3. B — y ÷ 4
   The key words tell us the operation. "a number y shared equally among 4 people" is written y ÷ 4.

4. B — 5 cm
   Subtract the start from the end: 10 − 5 = 5 cm.

5. A — 6 m 35 cm
   Change to centimetres: 460 + 175 = 635 cm = 6 m 35 cm.

6. C — 120 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. Use this to change between the two units: 1.2 m in centimetres is 120 cm.

7. A — 15 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 3 × 5 = 15 square units.

8. C — 36 square metres
   9 × 4 = 36 square metres.

9. B — Rectangle Q
   P = 5 × 7 = 35 and Q = 6 × 6 = 36. Rectangle Q has the bigger area.

10. A — 64 blocks
   One layer has 4 × 4 = 16 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 16 × 4 = 64 blocks.

11. A — 3
   Layers = 72 ÷ 24 = 3.

12. D — 1,000 cubic centimetres
   10 × 10 = 100 per layer and 100 × 10 = 1,000 cubic centimetres.

13. D — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

14. B — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

15. B — 3/4 kg
   0.75 = 75/100 = 3/4, so it is 3/4 kg.

16. D — 1/2 kg
   1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2.

17. B — 3 3/4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 6 kg − 2 1/4 kg = 3 3/4 kg.

18. C — from midnight to noon
   a.m. is used from midnight to noon and p.m. from noon to midnight.

19. D — 2 h 30 min
   150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30, so 150 minutes = 2 h 30 min.

20. B — 14 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 2 × 7 = 14 days.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: 10 3/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Total sold: 7 1/2 + 6 3/4 = 7 2/4 + 6 3/4 = 13 5/4 = 14 1/4 kg (3 marks). 25 − 14 1/4 = 10 3/4 kg (2 marks).

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Area is the amount of flat surface a shape covers, in square units. Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up, in cubic units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for area and 1 mark for volume.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 15 kg
   Working / marking points: 12 − 5 = 7 kg of beans (1 mark); 7 + 8 (1 mark); 15 kg (1 mark).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: The learner added. She should multiply: one layer has 4 × 3 = 12 blocks and 2 layers make 24 blocks.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the mistake, 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for 24 blocks.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the expression, 1 mark for 4m, 1 mark for 6o, 1 mark for the final answer.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) 6:30 a.m. (b) 3:15 p.m. (c) 7:30 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct time with a.m. or p.m.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 m 50 cm and 2.5 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dividing by 100, 1 mark for 2 m 50 cm, 1 mark for 2.5 m.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 5 − 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 150 minutes = 2 hours 30 minutes. 35 days = 5 weeks.
   Working / marking points: 150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30 (1 mark for 2 h 30 min); 35 ÷ 7 = 5 (1 mark for 5 weeks); 1 mark for division working.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6:00 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 4:20 + 1 h = 5:20 p.m. (1 mark); + 40 min = 6:00 p.m. (1 mark).
